newsitem.title: USA: Tucson Electric renegotiates coal contract.
newsitem.headline: Tucson Electric renegotiates coal contract.

text.p: Tucson Electric Power Co announced on Tuesday it had renegotiated a 13-year coal contract with Peabody Coalsales, a unit of Energy Group Plc, which will reduce annual fuel costs by around $10 million.
As part of a the settlement, TEP terminated its existing coal contract for the Springerville coal-fired power plant and entered into a new agreement with Peabody.
To terminate the original contract, TEP incurred a fee of $50 million.

The utility said it will apply to the Arizona Corporation Commission (ACC) for the fee to be treated as a regulatory deferred asset and amortized to fuel expense over the 13-year term of the new agreement.
If the ACC approves the request, the Company will realize net savings of $3.7 million annually, including amortization of the termination fee.
In the interim, TEP said it filed a request with the ACC to account for the payment as a deferred asset.

The ACC is not expected to hear the company's request for an interim accounting order until the end of July. In the event the ACC denies the requested accounting treatment, TEP may have to expense the $50 million immediately.
In addition to the new contract savings, TEP said it has saved $7.9 million annually in fuel expenses as a result of other fuel agreements that were renegotiated in 1995 and 1996.
